_comment: Editorial curation over the Wikidata P37 baseline. This pack teaches what people SPEAK in a place, not a language's legal status, so we use official languages as a guideline and correct the cases where P37 is a poor answer to 'what do they speak there?'. `remove` drops a (country, language) pair; `add` asserts one P37 omits. Both keyed by country Q-ID, valued by language Q-IDs. Adding a language here also makes this pack OWN its entity (fetch-entities resolves it). Keep this list small — P37 is right for ~all countries; only the flagrant misfits belong here.

_notes.Q30: United States: P37 lists only territorially-official languages (Carolinian, Chamorro, Hawaiian, Samoan) and Spanish, omitting English — the federal US designates none. Add English; keep Spanish (widely spoken); drop the four territorial-only entries that make 'a language spoken in the US' read as Carolinian.
_notes.Q77: Uruguay: no P37 value at all (Spanish is de facto, not de jure). Add Spanish.
_notes.Q423: North Korea: drop 'North Korean standard language' (Q18784), a bad Wikidata entity — it is just Korean (Q9176), which is already asserted.
_notes.Q1006: Guinea: drop 'languages of Guinea' (Q1339026), not a language at all — French (Q150) is already asserted.
